candidates.current: JSON and JSONC already expose bounded parsing, path entries, line-column locations, diagnostics, safe editing and source signature protection; production code has no schema provider, schema URI or mapping token
candidates.gap: a trusted local sidecar naming rule, bounded schema loading, JSON Schema draft support, instance-path-to-source mapping, diagnostic provenance and failure fallback are absent

candidates.current: YAML and TOML have bounded parsers and path outlines
candidates.gap: scalar conversion, tag and numeric fidelity, multi-document behavior and mapping semantics require an independent contract

candidates.current: XML has bounded parsing, namespaces, paths and DOCTYPE blocking
candidates.gap: XSD import/include resolution, namespace identity, external resource blocking and validator dependency are absent

candidates.current: community interaction remains a filtered subgraph rather than proxy collapse
candidates.gap: proxy identity, aggregated edges, history, evidence, minimap, export and camera restoration contracts are absent

candidates.current: notes remain parsed, indexed and read-only
candidates.gap: LibreOffice and PowerPoint producer preservation remains asymmetric

candidates.current: recency and relation-strength rings are accepted
candidates.gap: stable per-node governance facts, provenance and explanation are absent
